status: MEASURED on the corrected instrument, WEIGHTING UNIFIED after the audit (task-8 rework)
what_changed: the first version used a single global baseline and unit weights, while the plan-2.51 record used per-context leave-one-out with 1/(K*C). That convention mismatch is the whole of the 3x disagreement between the two committed "trusted" records (2100.6 vs 6403.7). Both now use the same LOO weighting, and the two records agree to 6% (tr(Sigma) 39.726 vs 39.888; ||g||^2 0.01891 vs 0.01782; kappa 2100.6 vs 2238.5).
headline: the defensible range is kappa ~ 125 (median per-context) to 218 (curve-implied), i.e. of order 10^2 rollouts per context for r=0.5. The POOLED estimate 2238 is ~10x higher and is not the like-for-like quantity: it mixes contexts whose per-rollout score scales differ, variation the split-half estimator cancels by comparing two halves of the same contexts. Only 5 of 8 contexts even have a positive signal estimate (g_sq > 0), which is itself a finding about n=256.
not_claimed: that two independent routes agree within 5% (deleted: it compared kappa against 2*kappa and two different estimators)
a single point value for kappa
that the estimator class is unusable
